statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the server has sent the greeting (welcoming) message and the client has received it, the client normally sends the EHLO command to the server, indicating the client's identity. In addition to opening the session, use of EHLO indicates that the client is able to process service extensions and requests that the server provide a list of the extensions it supports.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Older SMTP systems that are unable to support service extensions, and contemporary clients that do not require service extensions in the mail session being initiated, MAY use HELO instead of EHLO.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For a particular connection attempt, if the server returns a 'command not recognized' response to EHLO, the client SHOULD be able to fall back and send HELO.
statements.trigger: server returns command-not-recognized response to EHLO

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST NOT return the extended EHLO-style response to a HELO command.
